query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In the Co‐free FeNiCrMn alloy, the dynamic mechanical behavior across temperature and strain‐rate regimes is governed by a shift in the dominant plastic deformation mechanism. At lower strain rates and/or higher temperatures, conventional dislocation glide and dynamic recovery are prevalent, whereas at higher strain rates and/or lower temperatures, adiabatic heating limits recovery and enhances dislocation accumulation together with the onset of deformation twinning. This transition—enabled by a lower stacking fault energy in the absence of Co—sustains a favorable strength–ductility balance under dynamic loads.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn produced by conventional melting methods with a uniform casting microstructure.
generation.intervention: Perform a set of controlled dynamic compression tests varying both strain rate and temperature on identical as-cast FeNiCrMn samples.
generation.conditions: Samples will be tested under ambient pressure using a universal testing machine for quasi-static conditions (e.g. ~10^(-4) s^(-1)) and a split-Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) system for high strain rates (~1300 to 2100 s^(-1)). The temperature will be controlled over a defined range (e.g. room temperature to elevated temperatures) while all other variables (sample geometry, microstructure from casting) are held constant.
generation.structural_mediator: The accumulation of dislocations and the formation of deformation twins, quantified by microstructural analyses such as EBSD and TEM.
generation.mechanism: Under higher strain rates and/or lower temperatures, adiabatic heating promotes localized dislocation pile-up and triggers deformation twinning. In the Co-free alloy, the absence of Co affects stacking fault energy such that dynamic recovery is less pronounced, preserving a high dislocation density and twin fraction that together contribute to sustained work hardening without sacrificing ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in dynamic yield strength and strain-hardening rate with higher strain rates (or lower temperatures) will be observed, accompanied by a measurable increase in the density of deformation twins compared to quasi-static conditions; ductility remains on par with the as-cast baseline.
generation.baseline: The baseline is the known strength–ductility balance of as-cast FeNiCrMn alloy under quasi-static loading at room temperature.
generation.boundary: This mechanism is expected to control behavior in the as-cast FeNiCrMn state under dynamic compression within the tested ranges of strain rate (quasi-static to SHPB regimes) and temperatures (room to moderately elevated temperatures). It may not apply if the microstructure is significantly altered by severe plastic deformation or post-solidification anneals.
generation.uncertainty: While the combined role of dislocations and deformation twins is anticipated from alloy physics, the relative quantitative contributions of each mechanism under different test conditions remain uncertain and require detailed microstructural quantification.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of dynamic compression tests on identically prepared as-cast FeNiCrMn samples at both quasi-static strain rates and in the SHPB regime, across a range of temperatures. Pre- and post-deformation microstructural characterization (using EBSD and TEM) will quantify dislocation densities and twin fractions. Mechanical properties (dynamic yield strength, strain-hardening rate, and ductility) will be measured and correlated with the observed microstructural features.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tests do not show an increase in yield strength and strain-hardening rate with increasing strain rate (or a shift in mechanism evidenced by increased twin formation) and if ductility is significantly compromised compared to the quasi-static baseline, then the hypothesized mechanism is falsified.

The as-cast equiatomic NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy has a simple FCC crystallographic structure. Serration behavior is observed in the stress- strain curves of the as-cast NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy deformed at dynamic loadings. The yield strength of the high-entropy alloy, which distributes from 490 to 800 MPa, presents a positive relationship with the strain rates. The Johnson–Cook plastic model and the Zerilli–Armstrong plastic model of the NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy are obtained. However, the results predicted by Zerilli–Armstrong correspond better with the experimental results. The serration behavior of the NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy at a high strain rate is sensitive to the strain rates. The high density of deformation bands plays an important role in the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of the as-cast NiCrFeCoMn high-entropy alloy deformed at dynamic loadings.
